name: Polish shoes properly
blurb: A proper polish is clean, condition, colour, then shine — four steps, not one. Done well, it doubles the life of good leather shoes.
gear: Horsehair brushes, a cloth, cream polish and wax polish
steps: Remove the laces and brush off all dirt. Polishing over grit grinds it into the leather.
Clean with a leather cleaner or a damp cloth, and let the shoes dry fully.
Apply cream polish to nourish and colour the leather, working it in with a cloth and letting it sit.
Buff with a horsehair brush using fast, light strokes until an even sheen appears.
For a mirror shine on the toe cap, apply thin layers of wax with a damp cloth in small circles, building up gradually with a drop of water each time.
Insert shoe trees and rotate your shoes, giving each pair a day to dry out between wears.
tips: Thin layers, always. Thick wax cracks and flakes.
Shoe trees and a rest day do more for shoe longevity than polishing does.
Do not use wax on suede or nubuck — they need a completely different routine.
proof: A mirror shine on the toe cap you can see your reflection in, on shoes that were scuffed.
